category_title: Highly anxious students with bipolar disorder who thrive in low-pressure environments
student_description: Shirley is a 61-year-old student with bipolar affective disorder who carries severe trauma from past educational experiences, making her terrified of ridicule and highly sensitive to pressure. She uniquely requires an environment completely devoid of time or performance pressure, where teachers actively model vulnerability and explicitly guarantee that mistakes and mental health relapses are accommodated.

criteria.rationale: Shirley needs ongoing, explicit reassurance before and during the course that she will never be hurried or pressured, in order to feel safe enough to attend.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan includes proactive, explicit reassurances (e.g., before the course or before new modules) that the student will never be hurried or pressured.

criteria.rationale: Because her bipolar affective disorder makes her mental health precarious, she needs to know that absences won't result in losing her place.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan includes repeated, explicit guarantees that the student's place will be held open and accommodated if she experiences a mental health relapse.

criteria.rationale: Shirley fears being laughed at by 'normal people,' so the long-term environment must actively foster a sense of shared identity and non-judgment among peers.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan incorporates strategies to actively foster a non-judgmental group culture where the student feels accepted by her peers.
